modules.name: ClickUp OS — Foundation
modules.rung_label: rung 2 — extend ClickUp you already pay for
modules.problem: ClickUp is in the stack but used as a task tracker only. No brand-as-OS template, no multi-brand parent structure, no ScaleReady, no daily-checks. Every other module has nowhere to land without this.
modules.outcome: True OS. Brand-as-OS template (6 departments) × each brand. Three-stage NPD pipeline. Per-role Ad-Hoc Boards. ScaleReady Stage 1 for HR. Report Hub separation. The base layer everything else lands on.
prerequisites: Owner who'll maintain structure post-build (Cara or Sim)
key_metrics: All 7 module outputs land in ClickUp (target: 100%)
Team works from ClickUp not ad-hoc Slack threads (target: <10% ops conversations off-ClickUp)
Time-to-find-task target <30 sec from any team member
modules.week_after: Ideal Direct has one place work happens. Every module that follows has a home. Cara opens ClickUp Monday morning and sees recruitment, not Slack.

risks.risk: Team adoption — going from light-touch ClickUp to full OS is a big shift
risks.mitigation: Roll out one brand first (Pest X Pro), prove the win, expand

risks.risk: Structure rigidity — folder/list hierarchy locks in early decisions
risks.mitigation: Start with Sim's Ideal-Direct template; iterate after 4 weeks of use

modules.name: Recruitment Pipeline
modules.problem: Fully ad hoc recruitment. No ATS, no scoring rubric, no structured flow from job post to decision. Cara and Sim manage candidates from memory. Every unfilled brand manager role is a direct cap on growth — Sim's stated #1 bottleneck.
modules.outcome: n8n-orchestrated pipeline. Applications ingest automatically (form / email alias). Scoring rubric applied. ClickUp task per candidate in HR/Recruitment folder. Interview scheduling via n8n. Decision logged to Supabase. Sim exits the loop until shortlist. Cara owns the surface.
prerequisites: Scoring rubric agreed with Cara (1-day workshop)
Application intake form or email alias
key_metrics: Time from application to first-stage review (target: <48 hrs)
Sim hrs/week on recruitment admin (target: <1 hr/wk vs current ~5)
Pipeline visibility: any open role has 4+ candidates at various stages at all times
modules.week_after: Cara opens ClickUp Monday. 4 brand manager candidates at various pipeline stages — all auto-scored. Sim hasn't seen a CV. The Monday recruitment crisis call is gone.

risks.mitigation: Run first 3 candidates manually alongside the system; refine the rubric from real data
Cara helps design the rubric — ownership = adoption

modules.dependency_failure_mode: Without Module 01's HR/Recruitment folder structure, n8n posts have nowhere to land — candidate tasks scatter across Slack DMs and Cara's notes app. Build it first.

modules.name: Demand Planning
modules.rung_label: rung 4 — n8n + Supabase, glued to existing SP-API
modules.problem: Chris is the human reorder system. Gut-feel + Linnworks spot-checks. No system linking sell-velocity to reorder triggers. Overstock write-downs and OOS events on every new market launch.
modules.outcome: Supabase + n8n. Real sell-through from SP-API. Blended 7/14/30-day velocity. Reorder triggers at <21 days cover. ClickUp tasks assigned to Chris. Foundation for Module 04.
prerequisites: Chris available for onboarding (~6 hrs over 3 weeks)
key_metrics: OOS events per month (target: <2)
Overstock write-down value (target: -50% YoY)
Chris hrs/week on reorder decisions (target: <2 vs current ~6)
modules.week_after: Chris checks the Demand Forecast folder. Three ASINs flagged below 21 days cover, quantities and lead times calculated overnight. He approves reorders in 5 minutes.

risks.risk: Seller Central API rate limits hit during 14-day moving window calc
risks.mitigation: Cache intermediate results; run incrementally, not all-at-once

risks.risk: Brand managers resist owning the number — historically Chris's job
risks.mitigation: Roll out with one brand (Pest X Pro), prove the win, expand

modules.dependency_failure_mode: Without Module 01, reorder tasks have no Demand Forecast folder and Chris falls back to spreadsheet alerts — the velocity math runs but no one acts on it.

modules.name: PPC + Stock Interlock
modules.rung_label: rung 5 — Claude Code routine + n8n; retires Scale Insights
modules.problem: Scale Insights (~£300/mo) as a black-box PPC automation. Overbidding on near-OOS ASINs. SQPR keywords unactioned. Brand managers flying blind.
modules.outcome: Stock data from Supabase connected to PPC logic via n8n. ASINs under 14 days cover have bids suppressed automatically. SQPR harvested on schedule. Scale Insights retired.
prerequisites: Brand managers available for rubric input
key_metrics: Wasted ad spend on near-OOS ASINs (target: -90%)
SQPR harvest rate (target: weekly, all brands)
Scale Insights subscription cancelled (binary)
modules.week_after: Red checks PPC. Two Deer & Oak ASINs had bids automatically suppressed overnight because stock dipped. £200 in wasted spend that didn't happen.

risks.risk: Bid suppression too aggressive — kills sales on borderline ASINs
risks.mitigation: Configurable threshold per brand; start conservative (21 days cover); tighten over time

risks.risk: Scale Insights cancellation premature — features we're not replacing
risks.mitigation: Audit Scale Insights usage for 2 weeks before retiring; add anything missing

modules.dependency_failure_mode: Without Module 03's stock data in Supabase, the bid-suppression rules have nothing to read — Scale Insights stays in the loop and Red flies blind on near-OOS ASINs.

modules.name: Image Upload Automation
modules.rung_label: rung 2 — Figma plugin extending tool you already own
modules.problem: Simon's manual Figma → download → Seller Central ritual. 3-5 hrs/week minimum. Every listing launch constrained by one person's bandwidth. Mirrors Sim's #01 case study.
modules.outcome: Figma plugin → n8n → SP-API Listings endpoint. Simon pushes from Figma; n8n handles the rest. Human all but removed.
prerequisites: Simon involved in plugin UX (1 day)
key_metrics: Simon hrs/week on manual uploads (target: <30 min vs current ~4 hrs)
Listing launch time from Figma-complete to live (target: <15 min vs current ~half-day)
modules.week_after: Simon exports from Figma. The upload is live on Seller Central 10 minutes later without him touching Seller Central.

risks.mitigation: Plugin handles UX; n8n + SP-API does the heavy lifting

risks.risk: SP-API rate limits on bulk uploads

modules.name: SQL MCP · Self-Serve Reporting
modules.rung_label: rung 5 — Supabase + Claude SQL MCP; retires Power BI
modules.problem: Power BI (~£100/mo) gated through Franc only. Entire team waits for reports. If Franc leaves, reporting stops. Key-person risk flagged as existential.
modules.outcome: Supabase + Claude SQL MCP. Any team member queries live data in plain English via Claude Desktop. Franc transitions from gatekeeper to query expert. Report Hub in ClickUp.
prerequisites: Claude Desktop access for the team
key_metrics: Number of team members self-serving data (target: 8+)
Power BI subscription cancelled (binary)
Franc single-point-of-failure resolved (binary)
modules.week_after: Tom asks Claude 'which Pest X Pro ASINs are below average CVR in the last 30 days?' and has the answer in 20 seconds. Franc didn't need to be called.

risks.risk: Franc sees this as job displacement
risks.mitigation: Reframe his role: from gatekeeper to query expert + dashboard architect; he becomes more strategic, not less
Read-only connection; query timeout; Supabase indexes on hot columns

modules.dependency_failure_mode: Without Modules 03+04 data flowing into Supabase, the SQL MCP has nothing live to query — the team falls back to Franc + Power BI and the single-point-of-failure stays.

modules.name: Buybox + Competitive Monitor
modules.rung_label: rung 6 — new SaaS (Rainforest API) + n8n orchestration
modules.problem: Sim and Adam doing ad hoc pricing spot-checks. Pest X Pro competitors changing price overnight, discovered 3 days late. Margin leaking on the brand with the best competitive moat.
modules.outcome: Rainforest API → n8n → Supabase. Competitive position changes trigger ClickUp flags. Auto-reprice within defined bands. Pest X Pro and Deer & Oak protected.
prerequisites: Pricing band rules defined by Adam + Sim (1 day)
key_metrics: Time from competitor price change to detection (target: <12 hrs)
Buybox win rate on monitored ASINs (target: +10pp)
Margin delta on monitored ASINs (target: protect within 5% of target)
modules.week_after: Pest X Pro main ASIN flagged at 7am — competitor dropped price 8% overnight. Adam reviews and approves auto-reprice in 3 minutes. Previously this would have been discovered on Thursday.

risks.risk: Auto-reprice too aggressive — race to bottom
risks.mitigation: Hard margin floor; never let auto-reprice drop below break-even; daily reset on triggers

risks.risk: Rainforest API costs scale with ASIN count
risks.mitigation: Start with top 20 monitored; expand only if ROI proves

modules.dependency_failure_mode: Without Module 01, alerts have no Pricing folder to land in; without Module 03, alerts have no stock context — competitor changes still get missed for days even with the API hooked up.

featured_module_derivation.notes: Module 03 Demand Planning wins on ROI (£65k/yr — highest by 2.7×) at Intermediate complexity. Module 02 Recruitment remains the recommended-start (Sim's stated #1 bottleneck) but scores lower on the featured rubric due to Advanced complexity. F3 decouples featured (score-driven, biggest visible win) from recommended-start (sequencing, addresses stated bottleneck).

capacity_envelope.notes: All 7 modules fit comfortably; no capacity-fit drops fired. Headroom available for Phase-2 revisits or universal_opportunities follow-through.

recommendations.future_state_narrative: Twelve months from now, your Tuesday morning starts in ClickUp's brand-as-OS view. Pest X Pro shows three reorder candidates flagged overnight by Demand Planning — Chris approves in 5 minutes. Cara opens her recruitment list: 4 brand manager candidates at various stages, all auto-scored, ready for her shortlist. Red asks Claude in plain English which Deer & Oak ASINs underperformed PPC last week, gets the answer in 20 seconds. Simon pushes a Figma update; the listing's main image is live on Seller Central before he closes the laptop. Adam's 7am notification: a Pest X Pro competitor moved overnight; the auto-reprice held within margin. Franc shifted from Power BI gatekeeper to query architect. The team works from a system, not a gut feel. Recruitment is no longer the bottleneck — Rooted Human launched, US scaling started, Sim+Jack are spending time on strategy not Slack triage.
